plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Enormous, ruffled blooms with a rich, sweet perfume nod above glossy, deeply cut foliage. Each flower can open into a lush bowl of silky petals, often dotted with golden stamens at the center.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer, typically May through June
plants.location: Gardens across the temperate Northern Hemisphere, including the United States, Europe and northern China
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for more than 50 years in the same spot, and in China they have been cultivated for well over a thousand years.

plants.name: Rosa canina
plants.description: A graceful, arching wild shrub that tumbles through hedgerows with delicate, five-petaled flowers. The blooms release a soft, sweet fragrance, and they later give way to bright red hips.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer, with peak bloom in late May and June
plants.location: Hedgerows and woodland edges across Europe, including the British Isles, and parts of western Asia and northwest Africa
plants.funFact: Dog rose hips are packed with vitamin C. During World War II, Britons gathered them to make rose hip syrup when citrus fruit was scarce.

plants.name: Leptospermum scoparium
plants.description: A hardy, wind-sculpted shrub that is smothered in small, star-like flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, it brings color to the coastal scrub and hillsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly spring to summer in New Zealand, so late May falls outside the usual peak
plants.funFact: Bees that forage on mānuka produce the famous mānuka honey, which is prized for its unusual compounds.
